problem: The regression-to-the-mean sentence 'the predicted y lies closer to ȳ than x lies to x̄' compares a distance in y-units with a distance in x-units. Taken literally it is false: if y varies far more than x (σy much larger than σx) the predicted y can sit numerically further from ȳ than x sits from x̄. The true statement is about standard-deviation units.
fix: Write it in standardised form: (ŷ − ȳ)/σy = r (x − x̄)/σx, so |ŷ − ȳ|/σy = |r| |x − x̄|/σx < |x − x̄|/σx when |r| < 1. Say 'the predicted y lies closer to ȳ in standard-deviation units than x lies to x̄ in its own standard-deviation units'.

problem: 'The slope is less than the perfect-line slope' uses the term 'perfect-line slope' without ever defining it. A student cannot tell what number is being compared, and 'less than' is ambiguous for negative slopes.
fix: Define it once: when |r| = 1 the slope is σy/σx; in general b_yx = r σy/σx, so for |r| < 1 its magnitude is smaller than σy/σx, i.e. |b_yx| < σy/σx.
